text:
Recent product-recommendation research distinguishes substitutes from complements rather than treating all related products as equally useful; the [TREC 2025 recommendation task](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html) evaluates these relations separately. For this task, a proposed evidence-based taxonomy is: immediate relevance—specific support from recent history or supplied feedback; broad association—shared subject, function, or series without demonstrated current need; possible redundancy—overlapping function or edition, without assuming ownership satisfaction; explicit specification conflict—documented incompatible requirements; insufficient evidence—missing or ambiguous information. These are diagnostic judgments, not observed preference labels. Compatibility requires explicit specifications; interaction history alone cannot establish ownership, satisfaction, or rejection.

Annotation research supports retaining individual judgments and disagreement. [FLEAD (2024)](https://aclanthology.org/2024.tacl-1.35/) finds value in learning annotator perspectives rather than collapsing them into one majority label. [Crowd-Calibrator (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.14141) uses annotation disagreement to inform calibration and selective prediction on subjective language tasks. Applied here, record each judgment’s supporting history, title/description passage, timestamp, or qualitative feedback, alongside uncertainty and alternative interpretations. Agreement is useful evidence of consistency, but does not establish factual correctness or personal usefulness.

[Selective classification under distribution shifts (2024)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12470254/) studies abstention when predictions are likely wrong, including shifted inputs. Its practical implication here is to assess error versus coverage on independently reviewed judgments before trusting confidence thresholds. With only twenty users, treat feedback as hypothesis-generating: investigate recency weighting, redundancy penalties, or specification filters only where evidence supports them; retain uncertain cases without converting them into negative preferences. Select model changes using the prescribed macro validation HR@10, keeping diagnostic confidence separate from recommendation performance.
